bio: Amit runs network-wide supply-chain planning for decorative and adjacent categories. He cares about depot service levels, festive-season readiness, and whether a tool can sit next to the current SAP extracts.
responsibilities: Alignment between sales ops and plants
recent_activity: Spoke at an industry planning forum about consensus planning across sales and supply.
Internal mandate this year is cleaner festive-season readiness for top SKUs.
communication_style: Direct, numbers-first, impatient with generic digital-transformation language.
likely_pain_vs_product: NexusFlow Demand Planning is the fit: Amit already feels SKU-depot complexity and emergency transfers. He will reject anything that claims to replace SAP overnight.
talking_points: Depot emergency transfers and festive-season stockouts
Keep planners in control of the consensus plan
Works with existing SAP planning extracts
risks: May already be evaluating IBP or an internal model
Will ask for a tightly scoped pilot, not a platform tour
recommended_approach: Lead with a 20-minute working session on top-SKU festive readiness and emergency transfers. Do not open with a full suite demo.

bio: Kavita owns digital programs that touch dealer systems, data platforms, and supply tools. She is the likely internal champion if a vendor can prove it will not create another unused dashboard.
responsibilities: Digital roadmap for supply and channel systems
recent_activity: Posted on LinkedIn about making dealer and supply data usable for operators, not only data teams.
Reviewing which planning and channel tools can sit on existing extracts.
communication_style: Thoughtful, written, LinkedIn-comfortable. Prefers a crisp problem statement over a long pitch.
likely_pain_vs_product: She can champion Demand Planning and TradePulse if they reuse current extracts and give Amit and the channel team something they will actually open.
talking_points: Sit on existing SAP or DMS extracts
Operator-facing views, not another data lake project
Joint working session with supply and channel owners
risks: Will block tools that look like a second system of record
recommended_approach: Short LinkedIn note that names the dealer-and-planning data problem and asks if a joint session with supply chain is worth it.

bio: Rohan manages West region dealer performance. He lives in WhatsApp with dealers and influencers and is skeptical of head-office dashboards that arrive after the month is closed.
interests: Which dealers are actually slipping this week
Less weekend Excel from head office
recent_activity: Flagged delayed visibility on a few high-potential West dealers after a scheme change.
Uses WhatsApp as the default work channel with the field team.
communication_style: Informal, short, mobile-first. Will not read a long email.
likely_pain_vs_product: TradePulse is the product he would feel: live dealer health and program spend, not a planning-theory conversation.
talking_points: Week-level dealer health instead of month-end claims
Painter-program leakage
Mobile review for regional managers
risks: May see analytics as head-office surveillance if the tone is wrong
recommended_approach: One short WhatsApp note about West dealer visibility. Ask if a 15-minute look at two slipping outlets is useful. No brochure language.

bio: Deepak runs procurement and vendor onboarding. He has already asked prior vendors not to contact him directly and is a process blocker, not a champion.
recent_activity: Asked a previous planning-software vendor to stop direct outreach.
communication_style: Formal and brief when he responds at all.
likely_pain_vs_product: Not a fit for first-touch outreach. Any message should be suppressed.
risks: Outreach would damage the Asian Paints relationship
recommended_approach: Do not message. If the account moves, route through Amit or Kavita and procurement's official RFP path.

bio: Meera owns day-to-day performance at a major Tata Steel plant. She will only look at tools that help the shift huddle and will reject anything that asks her team to abandon the current MES.
interests: Tools her supervisors will actually use
recent_activity: Pushed for faster exception reviews after a bottleneck quarter.
Public plant-excellence comments focus on reliability, not software brands.
communication_style: Operational, skeptical of vendor slides, prefers a plant-specific example.
likely_pain_vs_product: PlantConnect is the only NexusFlow product that belongs in this conversation. Frame it as a visibility layer on the current stack.
talking_points: Same-shift downtime picture for the huddle
Does not replace MES
One bottleneck view for plant and central ops
risks: May already have a historian or APM evaluation
recommended_approach: Email with one plant-huddle use case. Ask for 20 minutes with her and Industry 4.0, not a generic digital-transformation pitch.

bio: Arjun leads Industry 4.0 programs and is the translator between plant heads and central digital. He is active in an internal Slack workspace used by the manufacturing-excellence group.
recent_activity: Internal thread on which visibility tools plant supervisors will actually open.
Evaluating layers that sit on current OT data rather than new systems of record.
communication_style: Crisp, Slack-native, allergic to long email threads.
likely_pain_vs_product: He can champion PlantConnect if it is positioned as a layer on the current MES and historian, with a plant-head huddle view.
talking_points: Layer, not rip-and-replace
Plant-head and central-ops views
Same-shift exception reviews
risks: Will ignore anything that sounds like a new MES
recommended_approach: Short Slack note in the manufacturing-excellence context. Offer a 15-minute compare against their current huddle workflow.

bio: Sneha owns channel sales performance and the health of the dealer and electrician network. She is measured on secondary sales and program ROI, not on IT architecture.
interests: Program spend that is not producing secondary sales
recent_activity: Asked for a cleaner view of inactive influencers after a program audit.
Expanding coverage in a few under-indexed geographies.
communication_style: Commercial and practical. Wants a clear 'so what' in the first paragraph.
likely_pain_vs_product: TradePulse matches her job: dealer health, influencer-program leakage, and regional-manager mobile review.
talking_points: Inactive influencer spend
Week-level dealer scorecards
New-geography channel design
risks: May believe the current DMS already covers this
Regional teams can resist anything that feels like surveillance
recommended_approach: Email that names inactive-influencer spend and slipping dealers. Ask for a 20-minute look at two regions, not a platform demo.

bio: Vikram runs IT and will be in the room if TradePulse needs DMS or identity integrations. He is not the commercial buyer and has not consented to SMS.
interests: Whether a tool creates a second system of record
recent_activity: Tightening vendor questionnaires for analytics tools that sit on sales data.
communication_style: Precise, risk-aware, email-only for first contact.
likely_pain_vs_product: Useful later for integration, not for first commercial outreach. If messaged, keep it to architecture fit and a pointer to Sneha.
talking_points: Sits on existing DMS extracts
Does not replace the dealer system
IT review after a commercial working session
risks: Will stall a deal if first touch is a product blast
SMS consent is false and must stay unused
recommended_approach: Only email if Sneha wants IT in the first meeting. Otherwise wait. Never SMS.
